## WebQuiz 2.0: rewritten in Go

WebQuiz 2.0 is a full rewrite of the program in Go. It is **one file with no other parts to install**: no Python, no pip. Your quizzes, your `webquiz.yaml`, your CSV files and your folders work as before. The HTTP API, the config keys and the quiz format are the same as in 1.19.

### Downloads

- **Windows** (10 or newer): `webquiz-windows-setup.exe` (installer) or `webquiz-windows.exe.zip` (portable).
- **macOS** (12 or newer): `webquiz-macos-apple-silicon.zip` (M1 and newer) or `webquiz-macos-intel.zip`.
- **Linux**: `webquiz-linux.zip` (64-bit PC), `webquiz-linux-arm64.zip` (Raspberry Pi 3, 4, 5 with a 64-bit system), `webquiz-linux-arm.zip` (older Raspberry Pi boards: Zero, 1, 2).
- **Documentation** as PDF: `webquiz-documentation-en.pdf` and `webquiz-documentation-uk.pdf`.

The `pip install webquiz` package is not published for 2.0. The old Python version stays at [oduvan/webquiz](https://github.com/oduvan/webquiz).

### What is different from 1.19

**Install and start**
- One binary per platform. Files live next to the program, as in the 1.19 binaries. Set `WEBQUIZ_BINARY_DIR` to use another folder. This is useful for a service, for example on a Raspberry Pi data partition.
- The browser opens the admin page when the program starts, as in the 1.19 binary.
- Minimum systems: macOS 12 and Windows 10.
- `webquiz --version` now prints the real version. 1.19 always printed `1.0.0`.
- `webquiz -d` on Windows now says that it is not supported. 1.19 crashed there.
- The "new version" message in the admin panel now looks at the releases of [oduvan/webquiz-go](https://github.com/oduvan/webquiz-go). 1.19 looked at PyPI.

**New look**
- All pages are rebuilt with React and Tailwind: the quiz, the admin panel, the file manager, live stats and the CSV table. They have the same features. The phone layout works as before (768 px wide and less).

**Checker code of text questions**
- Checkers now run in Starlark, a small Python-like language. Normal Python checkers keep working. This includes `assert` with a message, f-strings with formats, `**`, chained comparisons like `0 < x < 10`, `math`, `to_int`, `distance`, `direction_angle`, string methods, loops and your own functions.
- These do not work: `try` / `except`, `raise`, `class`, `import`, `with`, `global`, `bytes()` and `fail()`.
- `len()` and indexing of text count bytes, not letters. For Ukrainian text, use `len(list(user_answer))` and `list(user_answer)[0]`.
- A checker now stops after 2 seconds or when it uses too much memory, and the answer counts as wrong. In 1.19 a checker like `while True: pass` could hang the server.
- When a quiz loads, the log gets a warning for each checker that the new version cannot run. Check your text questions once after you update.

**Bugs of 1.19 that are fixed**
- `/admin`, `/files` and `/live-stats` without the last slash now open the page. 1.19 showed 404, so the link printed at start did not work.
- If switching to a quiz file fails, the running quiz stays. 1.19 cleared the students first.
- Answers that waited for the 5-second CSV write are now written when you switch quizzes and when the server stops. 1.19 lost them.
- Quiz names with a folder part are refused. 1.19 let a name like `..%2F` reach files outside `quizzes/`.
- Downloading a quiz archive with an empty folder no longer copies the `.zip` file into `quizzes/`.
- Saving the running quiz in the file manager restarts it, as the docs always said.
- Live stats show the total points of the new quiz right after a switch. 1.19 kept the old total until a reload.
- The tunnel config download from an IPv6 tunnel server works.
- A config value of the wrong type now works. For example, `master_key: 12345` or `port: "8080"` are read as the text or number you meant. In 1.19 a numeric master key made the admin login fail.
- The old admin page had 11 small bugs. The new page does not copy them. One example: "Save and continue" on `x.yaml` made `x.yaml.yaml`.

**Kept as in 1.19**
- The file manager page shows the whole `webquiz.yaml`, including `admin.master_key` and any `auth_header_token`, to every computer on the local network that opens `/files/`. Keep your network private.

### Docs

The user guide for [English](https://github.com/oduvan/webquiz-go/tree/master/docs/en) and [Ukrainian](https://github.com/oduvan/webquiz-go/tree/master/docs/uk) is updated, with new screenshots. It is also online at <https://oduvan.github.io/webquiz-go/>.
